RESIDUAL_SWEEP_METHOD.rule: AP5 in v1.0.1 promised a semantic residual sweep and was not executed. This amendment executes it.
RESIDUAL_SWEEP_METHOD.method: Every string leaf of v1.0.0, v1.0.1, and both companion manifests was extracted by a recursive walk (not a grep of clause ids), then tested against six patterns matching the family of obsolete semantics: (1) 'before the deployment exist(ed)/was created', (2) 'frozen before ... creation/deployment', (3) 'pre-recorded deployment id', (4) 'recorded ... Every hit was individually read in full context and classified below as SUPERSEDED (new text replaces old), QUALIFIED (old text is accurate on its own plane but was unqualified and is now plane-labelled), or DEMONSTRATED_NOT_OBSOLETE (already closed by v1.0.1, or historically accurate and not asserted as a controlling rule).

RETRY_IDENTITY_CONTRACT.status: ADDITIVE to ACT_IDENTITY_CONTRACT (v1.0.1). Does not supersede AIC-1..AIC-7; resolves a case they did not address.
RETRY_IDENTITY_CONTRACT.the_gap: PR201's DEPLOYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_BOUNDARY.BOUNDED_RETRY_RULE authorizes AT MOST ONE retry when five conjunctive conditions hold (BR-1..BR-5: the first attempt never reached READY; the failure was platform infrastructure, not application/configuration/coherence; no environment variable changed between attempts; the exact SHA is byte-identical between attempts; human confirmation is re-obtained). AIC-1..AIC-7 as written do not say whether the retry reuses the first attempt's act nonce or mints a new one, and AIC-5's one-to-one first-bound-wins rule, read literally, would treat a SECOND deployment bearing the SAME nonce as an inadmissible governance incident — which would wrongly flag a PR201-authorized retry as a violation of this artifact's own identity contract. This gap is resolved here rather than left for an execution lane to guess at.

AIC-8_retry_mints_a_distinct_chained_non.rule: A retry authorized under PR201 BOUNDED_RETRY_RULE MUST mint a NEW act nonce, distinct from the first attempt's. The retry's act record MUST additionally carry a field naming the first attempt's nonce as its predecessor, and MUST record, with evidence, that each of BR-1 through BR-5 was satisfied.
AIC-8_retry_mints_a_distinct_chained_non.platform_carriage: The retry deployment's metadata carries BOTH meta.uellix_governed_act_nonce (its own, new nonce) AND meta.uellix_governed_act_supersedes_nonce (the first attempt's nonce), so the chain is verifiable by re-reading the platform record alone, independent of the local act record.
AIC-8_retry_mints_a_distinct_chained_non.why_a_new_nonce_and_not_reuse: Reusing the first attempt's nonce would make the retry deployment a SECOND deployment bearing an EXISTING nonce, which AIC-5 correctly refuses as a governance incident when the second deployment appears WITHOUT authorization. A distinct, explicitly-chained nonce keeps AIC-5's one-to-one rule intact — it continues to catch an unauthorized redeploy or duplicate exactly as designed — while making the ONE PR201-authorized retry a legitimate, separately-identified act rather than a collision.
AIC-8_retry_mints_a_distinct_chained_non.the_first_attempt_s_binding_is_untouched: The first attempt's nonce remains bound to its own deployment id, which reached a terminal ERROR state and never READY. That binding is not erased, reused, or reassigned; it stands as the historical record of the failed attempt, and per PR201 and AIC-7 a deployment that never reached READY was never admissible as governed evidence regardless of this contract.

AIC-9_retry_count_ceiling_independent_of.rule: This grant authorizes AT MOST TWO total deployment-creation acts under one governed sequence: the first attempt, and the one PR201-authorized retry. A THIRD nonce chained to the same sequence — whether directly to the first attempt's nonce or transitively through the retry's — is REFUSED, regardless of whether BR-1 through BR-5 would otherwise appear satisfied, because PR201's BOUNDED_RETRY_RULE caps retries at one and a nonce mechanism cannot expand a count ceiling a frozen authority fixed.
AIC-9_retry_count_ceiling_independent_of.how_the_ceiling_is_checked: An act record whose predecessor field is itself populated (i.e., a retry-of-a-retry) is, by construction, a request for a second retry. It is refused at the act-record stage, before any deployment is triggered, without needing to re-evaluate BR-1..BR-5.
AIC-9_retry_count_ceiling_independent_of.fail_closed_on_broken_chain: If a retry's act record cannot establish an unbroken, single-hop chain to a first attempt that itself terminated in ERROR without ever reaching READY, the lane STOPS and does not create a retry deployment under this mechanism. A further act, if one is ever needed, requires a successor authority — exactly as PR201's own EXPIRY clause already requires once its single execution is consumed.

clarification_of_AIC5_scope.rule: AIC-5's one-to-one, first-bound-wins prohibition is UNCHANGED and governs any deployment sharing an EXISTING nonce with a prior deployment. It does not, and was never intended to, prohibit a retry that mints its OWN distinct nonce under AIC-8. This is a scoping clarification, not a supersession: AIC-5's text is correct as written and needs no amendment; only its application to the retry case needed spelling out.

CONFIRMATION_AND_SHA_REVERIFICATION_ORDE.status: CORRECTS the ordering prose in v1.0.1 AIC-1 and AIC-3, which compressed PR201's actual two-stage sequence into one step. Does not change any substantive obligation; both stages were already independently required by PR201 and by AIC-1(b)/(e) — this corrects only the SEQUENCE in which the amendment described them.
CONFIRMATION_AND_SHA_REVERIFICATION_ORDE.the_imprecision: v1.0.1 ACT_IDENTITY_CONTRACT.AIC-3.ordering read: 'nonce recorded -> human confirmation -> deployment created -> id returned -> id bound to nonce.' This implies the human confirmation happens immediately before deployment creation. It does not: per PR201 HUMAN_CONFIRMATION.placement, the confirmation is obtained ONCE, before AUTH-1 (the environment-variable binding mutation) — a step that happens BEFORE the deployment is triggered under AUTH-2, and PR201 SB-3 requires a SEPARATE, second SHA re-verification immediately before the deployment trigger, which the v1.0.1 ordering did not mention at all.
the_corrected_sequence: 1. SB-1: git fetch and freeze SHA_FROZEN from origin/integration/commercial-v1.
2. The governed act record is opened: act nonce minted, SHA_FROZEN and the intended mechanism recorded, timestamped.

3. HUMAN_CONFIRMATION is obtained ONCE, per PR201's prompt_requirements, covering the whole sequence including 'exactly one deployment will be produced' — SB-2 states SHA_FROZEN verbatim in this same prompt.
4. AUTH-1 executes: the three branch-scoped Preview environment variables are bound.

5. SB-3: immediately before triggering the deployment, origin/integration/commercial-v1 is re-derived. If it differs from SHA_FROZEN, STOP_STALE — no deployment is triggered, and this contract's act record is closed as ABANDONED, not as a failed attempt eligible for AIC-8/AIC-9's retry chain, because BR-4 (byte-identical SHA) was never reached.
6. AUTH-2 executes: the deployment is created, carrying meta.uellix_governed_act_nonce (AIC-2).
7. SB-4 / AIC-3: the returned deployment id is captured and bound to the nonce within the same act.
8. AIC-4: the deployment record is re-read and the nonce is verified to have round-tripped exactly.
CONFIRMATION_AND_SHA_REVERIFICATION_ORDE.why_this_matters_to_retry: The retry path (AIC-8/AIC-9) begins at step 2 with a NEW nonce and its own human reconfirmation (BR-5) at step 3 — it does not re-run AUTH-1, because BR-3 requires no environment variable to have changed between attempts. Without this corrected sequence, it would not be clear whether a retry needs a second AUTH-1; it does not, and the corrected ordering makes that explicit by separating AUTH-1 (once) from AUTH-2 (the act that can be retried once).
